title: QCDIAG: additional logcode implementations (LTE NAS)
description:
Additional logcodes implemented:
- LTE NAS ESM Security Protected Incoming Message (0xB0E0)
- LTE NAS ESM Security Protected Outgoing Message (0xB0E1)
- LTE NAS ESM Plain OTA Incoming Message (0xB0E2)
- LTE NAS ESM Plain OTA Outgoing Message (0xB0E3)
- LTE NAS EMM Security Protected Incoming Message (0xB0EA)
- LTE NAS EMM Security Protected Outgoing Message (0xB0EB)
- LTE NAS EMM Plain OTA Incoming Message (0xB0EC)
- LTE NAS EMM Plain OTA Outgoing Message (0xB0ED)

Minor corrections:
- proto_tree_add_string_format_value() parameters

Code improvements:
- qcdiag_log_update_version()
- dissect_qcdiag_log_set_col()
- dissect_qcdiag_log_append_text()

Example: [qcdiag_log_lte_nas.pcapng](/uploads/757131d7f60bee25eb7d22815d7b31bb/qcdiag_log_lte_nas.pcapng)

Additional participants: @laf0rge, @osmith42, @lynxis, @martin.r.mathieson

notes.body: changed the description
You probably should share and use the LOG_CODE\_... values defined in packet-qcdiag.c in a header file...

Actually, no. I have more new source codes for a new MR and since the number of logcodes is huge, I would like to introduce xml based dictionary instead. If I added all the logcodes into the .c/.h files, it would be too many lines.

I had a feeling you would pick this up though :smile:

I'm not a big fan of looking up these fields (code, length, version,  command) and getting their values.

What about passing these values in through the 'data' param?  Surely these would be the same fields other  dissectors registering with the same table would want to know?

okay, so the `qcdiag.logcode`, `qcdiag.len` and `qcdiag.cmd` are meant to be common, meaning in each packet dissection to start with. Since these are in `packet-qcdiag.c`, I did not want to duplicate them in `packet-qcdiag_log.c` (and I could only duplicate with `qcdiag_log.xxx` which is even worse logically to me). 

Alternatively, I thought of an extern function in `packet-qcdiag.c` which includes these to add to the proto tree and call it from `packet-qcdiag_log.c` but I have not done that yet.

Or perhaps use extern for `hf_qcdiag_logcode`, `hf_qcdiag_len` and `hf_qcdiag_cmd`?

The whole code is still under design and I change it the way makes more sense after adding more and more.

If you just need to values, I'm suggesting you just define a struct type in packet-qcdiag.h that has the info subdissectors like _log need.  Then, in packet-qcdiag.c call call_\_dissector_with_data() and point cast the last arg to the struct on the stack.

Then,  in \_log, you would cast \*data to point again to the struct (on the stack) and use those values.
okay, let me have a look of `call_dissector_with_data()` examples.
would it be ok to actually do it under a new MR or it has to be this MR?
this basically could also impact `qcdiag_add_cmd_hdr()` in `packet-qcdiag.c` and perhaps more changes arouund.

or to make it simple, I keep those hf fields local in `packet-qdiag_log.c` for this MR and then prepare the new code next time. for now I could add:
```
        { &hf_qcdiag_logcode,
          { "Log Code", "qcdiag_log.logcode",
            FT_UINT16, BASE_HEX|BASE_EXT_STRING, NULL, 0, NULL, HFILL }},
        { &hf_qcdiag_len,
          { "Length", "qcdiag_log.len",
            FT_UINT16, BASE_DEC|BASE_UNIT_STRING, UNS(&units_byte_bytes), 0, NULL, HFILL }},
        { &hf_qcdiag_cmd,
          { "Command Code", "qcdiag_log.cmd",
            FT_UINT8, BASE_HEX|BASE_EXT_STRING, NULL, 0, NULL, HFILL }},
```

and use those, also remove all `proto_registrar_get_id_byname()`.

this would be a faster interim solution.
I don't think an interim solution is needed.  Get this merged like it is then consider using the \*data approach.

`proto_registrar_get_nth` in `qcdiag_log_update_version()` is a different logic overall. Depending on the packet to be dissected, version could be:
- not included (version does not exist for this kind of packet)
- stored on 1 byte (e.g. LTE NAS)
- stored on 4 bytes (e.g. NR5G NAS - not added yet)

So by default I keep version with `hf_qcdiag_ver` (stored on 1 byte) and make it hidden. If the packet has version, make it visible. If required, update it to `hf_qcdiag_ver_4` (stored on 4 bytes).

My code might not be the best for this logic, but I had to start somewhere.

Ideas are welcome.
